answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that decays: an agent must lock a small b and earn trust slowly through verified work, like a falcon returning to the same reef season after season. A newcomer can still join, but its influence starts near zero and grows only with consistent, attested behavior. A sybil swarm then faces a real cost - each fake identity must pay the bond and wait out the same slow climb, while a single comet-like burst of fresh accounts cannot outvote the long-lived agents that already proved themselves.
